Check reported statistics against each other

Source: R/check_reported.R
check_reported.Rd

Takes the numbers a paper reports for an analysis and tests whether they can all be right at once, given how precisely they were reported ("2.85" means anything from 2.845 to 2.855). Where one input is missing but the output is reported, it gives the range the missing input must lie in.

Usage

check_reported(
  ...,
  test,
  variants = NULL,
  mu = 0,
  dims = NULL,
  p0 = NULL,
  effect = NULL,
  k = NULL
)

Arguments

...

Reported numbers, named by quantity (see quantity_names()). Pass strings, so the decimals count: t = "2.85", p = "< .001", df = "29". A quantity with one value per group or condition is a character vector (m = c("5.1", "4.2")). Integer-valued numbers are taken as exact.

For "mediation" (a simple, regression-based mediation, as in PROCESS model 4), a quantity with one value per path is a character vector named by path, a (X to M), b (M to Y), c (X to Y) and c_prime (X to Y with M held constant; c' is accepted): b, se, t, p, df, ci_lower, ci_upper and beta (for example ci_lower = c(a = "26.50", b = "-0.05")). The coefficient of a path is b, so b = c(a = "46.16", b = "-0.03") is the path a and the path b. n is a single string. The indirect effect is indirect; its bootstrap interval (indirect_ci_lower, indirect_ci_upper) is accepted but cannot be checked. When a, b and indirect are all reported, indirect is checked for coherence with a times b: it must lie in the product of the rounding intervals of a and b. This is arithmetic on the printed numbers and says nothing about significance; a bootstrap mean reported instead of the sample a times b is one possible reason for a mismatch. Two further arguments are read from ... for a mediation: indirect_type ("unstandardized", "standardized" or "partially_standardized"; a standardized indirect effect is only checked with beta for a and b, a partially standardized one is not evaluable) and estimator ("sem", "ml" or "lavaan" for numbers from an ML/SEM fit, which are not evaluable as a regression).

test

The test the numbers come from, in the vocabulary of sufficient_stats(): "student", "welch" (two independent groups; the name fixes the variant), "one_sample", "paired", "pearson", "oneway", "factorial", "chisq", "gof", "mediation" and "lm" (a multiple regression; "lm_simple" and "lm_moderation" for a simple regression and a moderation analysis). It can be given by name or as the first unnamed argument. Any other value is refused with the list of valid ones.

variants

Character vector restricting which variants to try (such as "two.sided", "0.95" or "welch"), or NULL for all. Each value restricts only its own kind of variant (tail, confidence level, test, convention): c("welch", "0.95") fixes the test and the level. A kind that no value names keeps all its variants. The accepted values are the codes below; the printed output shows a readable label instead. A value the handler does not have is an error that lists the ones it has.

  • Tail: "two.sided", "less", "greater" (shown as two-sided, one-sided (less), one-sided (greater)).

  • Level: "0.90", "0.95", "0.99" (shown as 90%, 95%, 99%).

  • Test: "student", "welch" (shown as Student's t, Welch's t).

  • SS type (factorial ANOVA, unbalanced designs): "III", "II", "I" (shown as type III, type II, type I).

  • Effect-size convention: "pooled" (Cohen's d, pooled SD), "hedges_g", "average" (Cohen's d, root mean square of the SDs), "glass_sd1", "glass_sd2" (Glass's delta), "cohen", "d_z", "d_rm", "d_av", "g_av", "eta2" (eta squared), "omega2" (omega squared), "partial_eta2", "partial_omega2" (factorial ANOVA). Which of them a handler has depends on the test.

mu

The test value the mean (or mean difference) is compared with, for tests whose t depends on it ("one_sample", "paired"). A plain number, not a string (mu = 20, not mu = "20"), unlike the reported numbers. Default 0. A test without a test value errors on mu other than 0.

dims

For "chisq", "gof" and "factorial", the table shape: c(rows, columns) for a test of independence, the number of categories for goodness of fit, the levels of each factor for a factorial design. Not needed when n is a matrix (its dim() is read before the counts are parsed). Without a shape df cannot be checked, because a flat vector of counts does not say whether 12 cells are 2 x 6 or 3 x 4.

p0

For "gof", the H0 proportions, one per category, summing to 1 (within 1e-8). Without them the categories are taken as equally likely.

effect

For "factorial", the effect to check: "A" (the factor in the rows of the cell matrices), "B" (the columns) or "AB" (the interaction). A paper with three F tests gets three calls with the same cell descriptives.

k

For the regression tests ("lm" and the like), the number of predictor columns (the model's df1), when F is not reported to say it. With k, n and df2 are checked against each other (df2 = n - k - 1) and either gives the other; without it they are not, because k is never guessed from the number of coefficients reported (a paper may leave some out). A plain number.

Value

A reprokit_check object: $numbers (status of each reported number), $level (coverage, 0 to 3), $missing (what would raise the level, and the range implied for it), $variants (a list with one data frame per kind of variant the handler has, each of the variants tried and whether they fit: tail, level, test (Student or Welch) and convention (how an effect size was computed)), $relations (one row per relation and variant; $variant and $kind join the values and kinds of a relation that varies over several with "+", and there is one column per kind, tail, level, test, convention, holding the row's value or NA), $implied, $implied_inputs (numbers derived from reported ones, such as n from df) and $checked (whether any relation that can falsify was compared with a reported number; without one there is no verdict).

The reported numbers come from one analysis, so they share one test and one confidence level: a variant fits only if one choice per kind explains every relation that can falsify. A CI whose bounds fit different levels, or a t that fits only Student next to a CI that fits only Welch, is inconsistent even though each relation holds on its own.

Some relations cannot falsify: how d was computed (pooled SD, average SD, Glass) is rarely declared, so a d that no convention reproduces gets the status "not reproducible", never "inconsistent", and $consistent is not affected.

A reported number is only ever compared within what it can be: r lies in -1 to 1, sd and df are not negative, p is in 0 to 1, n is a whole number. A relation whose result is not finite for the reported values ("1.00" for r gives an infinite t) is skipped, as if an input were missing; it never counts as a failure.

When n is not reported but df is, n is derived from df for the handlers where that is exact (a correlation, a paired or one-sample t): it is used by the other relations, shown as $implied_inputs, and counts for the coverage level, but df is never checked against it.

Examples

check_reported("paired", n = "20", t = "2.85", df = "19", p = ".010")
#> The analysis is consistent with the reported statistics.
#> Level 1: internal coherence only (statistic, df, p and CI are checked against each other, not against the descriptives).
#> Variants that fit: two-sided
#> 
#>  quantity reported   status     checked_against
#>         n       20 coherent           df_from_n
#>         t     2.85 coherent            p_from_t
#>        df       19 verified df_from_n; p_from_t
#>         p     .010 coherent            p_from_t
#> 
#> An inconsistency shows the numbers cannot all be correct as reported, not which one is wrong or why.

# A 2 x 2 table: Yates' correction is a variant, V is a convention
check_reported("chisq", n = matrix(c("30", "10", "20", "40"), 2), chisq = "15.04",
               df = "1", p = ".0001", v = ".41")
#> The analysis is consistent with the reported statistics.
#> Level 3: the sufficient set is reported (the numbers contain everything needed to reproduce the analysis; that is not itself a check).
#> Tests that fit: Yates' continuity correction
#> Effect-size conventions that fit: none
#> 
#>  quantity       reported   status                              checked_against
#>         n 30, 10, 20, 40 coherent chisq_from_table; p_from_table; v_from_table
#>     chisq          15.04 verified chisq_from_table; df_from_dims; p_from_chisq
#>        df              1 coherent                   df_from_dims; p_from_chisq
#>         p          .0001 verified                   p_from_table; p_from_chisq
#>         v            .41 verified                                 v_from_table
#> 
#> An inconsistency shows the numbers cannot all be correct as reported, not which one is wrong or why.

# A regression reports a number per coefficient: name them.
# A simple mediation (mpg ~ wt through hp): the paths, and the indirect effect
# checked for coherence with a times b
check_reported("mediation",
               b = c(a = "46.16", b = "-0.03", c = "-5.34", c_prime = "-3.88"),
               se = c(a = "9.63", b = "0.01", c = "0.56", c_prime = "0.63"),
               t = c(a = "4.80", b = "-3.52", c = "-9.56", c_prime = "-6.13"),
               n = "32", indirect = "-1.46")
#> The analysis is consistent with the reported statistics.
#> Level 1: internal coherence only (statistic, df, p and CI are checked against each other, not against the descriptives).
#> 
#>    quantity reported        status                 checked_against
#>         b:a    46.16      coherent t_from_b_se:a; indirect_from_ab
#>         b:b    -0.03      coherent t_from_b_se:b; indirect_from_ab
#>         b:c    -5.34      coherent                   t_from_b_se:c
#>   b:c_prime    -3.88      coherent             t_from_b_se:c_prime
#>        se:a     9.63      coherent                   t_from_b_se:a
#>        se:b     0.01      coherent                   t_from_b_se:b
#>        se:c     0.56      coherent                   t_from_b_se:c
#>  se:c_prime     0.63      coherent             t_from_b_se:c_prime
#>         t:a     4.80      coherent                   t_from_b_se:a
#>         t:b    -3.52      coherent                   t_from_b_se:b
#>         t:c    -9.56      coherent                   t_from_b_se:c
#>   t:c_prime    -6.13      coherent             t_from_b_se:c_prime
#>           n       32 not checkable                               -
#>    indirect    -1.46      coherent                indirect_from_ab
#> 
#> An inconsistency shows the numbers cannot all be correct as reported, not which one is wrong or why.

# A regression reports a number per coefficient: name them.
check_reported("lm", b = c(wt = "-3.88", hp = "-0.03"), se = c(wt = "0.63", hp = "0.01"),
               t = c(wt = "-6.13", hp = "-3.52"), p = c(wt = "< .001", hp = ".001"),
               r2 = ".83", f = "69.21", df1 = "2", df2 = "29", n = "32")
#> The analysis is consistent with the reported statistics.
#> Level 1: internal coherence only (statistic, df, p and CI are checked against each other, not against the descriptives).
#> Effect-size conventions that fit: R²
#> 
#>  quantity reported   status                                 checked_against
#>      b:wt    -3.88 coherent                                  t_from_b_se:wt
#>      b:hp    -0.03 coherent                                  t_from_b_se:hp
#>     se:wt     0.63 coherent                                  t_from_b_se:wt
#>     se:hp     0.01 coherent                                  t_from_b_se:hp
#>      t:wt    -6.13 coherent                     t_from_b_se:wt; p_from_t:wt
#>      t:hp    -3.52 coherent                     t_from_b_se:hp; p_from_t:hp
#>      p:wt   < .001 coherent                                     p_from_t:wt
#>      p:hp     .001 coherent                                     p_from_t:hp
#>        r2      .83 coherent                                       f_from_r2
#>         f    69.21 coherent                                       f_from_r2
#>       df1        2 coherent                                       f_from_r2
#>       df2       29 verified p_from_t:wt; p_from_t:hp; f_from_r2; df2_from_n
#>         n       32 coherent                                      df2_from_n
#> 
#> An inconsistency shows the numbers cannot all be correct as reported, not which one is wrong or why.
